$comment: Single source of truth for every editor-side Beans language asset.
The compiler owns this data. Each list below records where it comes from
in the beans repository so `npm run sync -- --beans <path>` can prove the
two are still in step. Do not hand-edit a generated file; edit this one
and run `npm run generate`.
Language intelligence (completion, hover, diagnostics, ...) is NOT here.
That lives in `beansc lsp` and reaches editors over LSP.

language.name: Beans
language.$comment: beans.pot is an exact filename. `.pot` is gettext's; never claim the suffix.

$comment: The 33 reserved spellings, in declaration order, straight from the
compiler's keyword table. `unique` and `super` are contextual and live
in contextualKeywords below.

deprecated.take: Reserved and lexed, but the parser rejects it: "'take' was removed — use 'move'". See beans/compiler/bootstrap/parser.cpp — parse_unary().

$comment: Not reserved — an ordinary identifier in any other position. Highlight
them, but never treat them as reserved words.
`recognizedWhen` is the exact shape the compiler's parser tests for.
It is the contract for every generated highlighting rule: outside that
shape the word is a name, and painting it as a keyword is a bug. The
compiler's own sources are the proof — `beans/src/module.b` has a
local called `package`, `beans/src/layout.b` a field called
`align` — so any rule that over-matches breaks the compiler's own
highlighting.
contextualKeywords.source: beans/spec/SYNTAX.md — 'Keywords and modifiers', 'Decided'; beans/src/parser.b — parse_declaration_body(), parse_member(), parse_statement(), parse_named_import()

recognizedWhen.brew: immediately before a call, as a statement or a `let`/`var` initializer — `brew warm(ctx)`; the `TaskGroup` method reads `group.brew(...)` and stays a method name
recognizedWhen.align: immediately before `(` — `align(8)`; a field named `align` reads `align:`
recognizedWhen.feature: immediately before a string literal — `feature "aes" fn`
recognizedWhen.package: `package <name>`, before every import and declaration in a file
recognizedWhen.super: a receiver inside a method of a class that extends another
recognizedWhen.priv: immediately before the name it restricts — `priv seen: int`, `priv fn step()`; a field named `priv` reads `priv:` or `priv =` and stays a name
recognizedWhen.abstract: immediately before `class` (with the other class modifiers) or before `fn`
recognizedWhen.partial: immediately before `class`, alone or with the other class modifiers
recognizedWhen.singleton: immediately before `class`, alone or with the other class modifiers
recognizedWhen.weak: a field declaration — `weak next: Option<Node>`; a field named `weak` reads `weak:`
recognizedWhen.const: `const <NAME>` at the start of a module-level declaration — `const LIMIT: int = 128`; a local or field named `const` stays a name
recognizedWhen.from: after an import list's closing `}` — `import {a, b} from crema.flex`

notKeywords.$comment: Called out because they look like keywords in other languages but are ordinary names in Beans. `while` is refused with a message naming `for` when it is written as a loop, so it is never painted as one either.

operators.$comment: Longest-match order preserved; a generator must not reorder these.

statements.$comment: Go-style: a newline ends a statement only after a token that can end one, so `} else {` must be on one line.

$comment: The compiler is the only language engine. Editor clients must not add a
second one — they negotiate these capabilities over LSP and render them.
The two compiler implementations advertise different legends today.
Editors must not hardcode either one — they negotiate the legend at
initialize. `all` is the union, and it is what the clients ship style
mappings for, so whichever build a user has, every token type the
server sends already has a style.
The invariant the test enforces is a subset check: every type the
running server advertises must appear in `all`. See
editors/test/lsp-smoke.test.mjs.

bootstrap.source: historical: the C++ bootstrap's lsp.cpp, which no longer exists. Kept because a user on an older build still negotiates this legend.

semanticTokens.$modifiersComment: `declaration` and `static` are LSP's own names. `private` is not — Beans has a visibility LSP has no modifier for, so the server sends one and the VS Code extension declares it under contributes.semanticTokenModifiers.

$comment: The C++ stage-0 server is bootstrap-only and advertises the original,
smaller set. Clients negotiate at initialize and must not assume either
list; this one records what the older server still answers so a user on a
stage-0 build gets no broken menu entries.
`@name` and `@pkg.name`, optionally with named arguments, written
above the declaration they describe. The compiler parses them in
parse_annotations(); arguments are always `name: expr`.
Two forms. `import pkg.path [as name]` binds the package;
`import {a, b as c} from pkg.path` binds the names and never binds
the package. An import list cannot take a trailing `as` — the alias
goes inside the braces.
